title: What an Animal Owes You
sentences: People describe their pets in language borrowed from friendship.
The comparison is understandable and only partly accurate.
A friendship assumes that both parties could walk away.
An animal in a house has no such option available to it.
This does not make the affection false, but it does change its shape.
What the animal gives is attention rather than agreement.
It does not care what I do for a living or how the week went.
Whole days can pass without any need to explain myself.
That may be the most restful thing about the arrangement.
The obligation, in the end, runs almost entirely one way.
